handover.title: Structure CW 2.0 Interaction, Spatial and Context Projection Decisions
handover.purpose: Consolidated decisions from the current Structure development session, intended as implementation guidance and handover context.
handover.primary_goal: Finish Structure sufficiently to use it for AIGMos 2.0 documentation canonicalization into CW 2.0.

core_role.description: Structure is not merely a CW visualizer. Its fundamental operation is selection and projection of a CW subgraph.
pipeline: optionally serialize the same subgraph as a CW bundle

shared_projection_model.principle: Visual projection and AI context projection operate on the same resolved CW subgraph.

relation_depths.description: Traversal depth is independently configurable by link type.

subgraph_selection.principle: A Structure projection preset can also function as an AI context preset.

canonical_base_format.description: The normal CW representation is one self-contained JSON document.

entity_file_projection.description: A monolithic CW document can be deterministically exploded into entity-oriented files for working storage and version control.
entity_file_projection.rule: Entity-per-file is not a separate CW format. It is a filesystem representation of the same CW data.

bundle.description: Entity files or selected entities can be bundled back into a monolithic CW document.

bundle.closure.description: Bundle selected entities plus the graph context resolved through configured relation-specific traversal depths.

bundle.invariant: Splitting and rebundling must preserve canonical semantics.

ai_context_use.description: A bot can request only the entities required for a task and receive them as one compact CW file.

node_position.decision: Entity nodes may carry canonical position information.
node_position.semantics: Position describes where the entity node exists within its referenced coordinate space.
node_position.rule: Position must not be hard-coded as screen or pixel coordinates.

coordinate_spaces.reason: The same position mechanism must support abstract diagrams and later physical/spatial projections.

recursive_composition.principle: An imported abstraction retains its own local coordinate space and can be anchored into a parent coordinate space.

map_projection.description: A Site-level entity can later be positioned geographically while its imported/internal abstraction continues using normal local or abstract coordinates.
map_projection.principle: Internal entities do not individually require GPS coordinates merely because their containing Site is shown on a map.

cad_projection.description: A Structure view may use a CAD drawing as a spatial background layer and place CW nodes over it.
cad_projection.principle: Nodes belong to the coordinate space, not to the CAD file itself.
cad_projection.benefit: A CAD revision can be replaced without redefining canonical node positions if the coordinate-space mapping remains valid.

box_behavior.purpose: Allow selection to be sculpted repeatedly using boxes and individual node toggles.

workflow_example: Create coarse selection with a box.
Toggle individual nodes for final adjustment.

terminology.description: Dependency, relation, ownership and other graph relations are all links. Their semantic type is defined separately.

zero_nodes_selected.visual: May use disabled or neutral state.

one_or_more_nodes_selected.behavior: Selected nodes form the source working set for link creation.

color_feedback.description: The Link control may change color according to the active link type/ruleset color space.

batch_creation_example.result: Create dependency links from the selected nodes according to the dependency link semantics.

multi_link_editing.description: Multiple links can be selected from the link list and edited as a batch.
multi_link_editing.preferred_apply_behavior: Validate the batch before committing the changes.

example.user_action: Set B as owner of X

ruleset_direction.description: Cardinality and replacement behavior should be expressed through the link ruleset rather than hard-coded specifically into Structure.

node.constraint: Deletion must not leave invalid dangling canonical references.

deletion.ui_principle: Nodes are spatial canvas objects. Links and events are primarily managed through their existing left-side list views.

node_merge.reason: Documentation canonicalization will reveal multiple entities that actually represent the same canonical concept.
pipeline: rewrite references from merged entities to survivor

reference_rewrite.principle: Merging is not equivalent to simply deleting duplicate entities. References must be redirected to the surviving canonical entity.

deduplication_and_conflicts.principle: Duplicate and conflict are different states.

identity_rule.description: Different object IDs may still represent semantically identical links or events.

events.rule: Event canonical-equivalence comparison must be strict because even small differences may change behavior.

aigmos_2_0_dependency.problem: AIGMos 2.0 scope is already locked, but its documentation must be canonicalized into CW 2.0.
aigmos_2_0_dependency.risk: The amount of documentation restructuring is large even though CW 2.0 can already express the required architecture.
aigmos_2_0_dependency.structure_role: Structure becomes tooling for performing the canonicalization efficiently instead of manually reconstructing the entire documentation set.

implementation_priority.feature: semantic duplicate detection for links and events

design_principles: Keep CW 2.0 monolithic JSON as the basic interchange and authoring format.
Treat entity-per-file storage as a deterministic projection, not a separate format.
Use the same graph traversal mechanism for Structure visualization and AI context generation.
Keep selection semantics extremely small: toggle.selection.
Keep input bindings separate from operations.
Use link as the generic term for graph relations.
Derive link behavior from rulesets where possible.
Do not allow UI operations to create structurally invalid CW.
Treat ownership as a single-parent hierarchy relation.
Treat a new ownership assignment as replacement, not addition.
Different IDs do not imply different semantics.
Identical links and events are duplicates, not conflicts.
Small semantic differences in events must be preserved.
Node merge must rewrite references rather than merely delete duplicates.
Do not bind node.position to screen coordinates.
Design coordinate spaces now so future maps, CAD views and physical spatial models do not require a CW migration.
Keep imported abstractions in their own local coordinate spaces and anchor them recursively into higher-level spaces.
Structure selection and projection should be directly reusable as controlled q/qc/agent context.

conceptual_core.summary: The same canonical CW graph and subgraph-selection mechanism serves both human Structure views and machine AIGMos context.
